203NoteBREAKTHROUGH: surprise field = 2*(measured - model). So surprise/2 gives measured-model directly. Confirmed on m1 (c0 82-79.81=2.19=4.38/2), m2, etc. Ambient: from m2 (min power) meas ~47, model@42 ~45.78 => real ambient ~43.2. At min power everything matches => healthy at low power. DECISIVE lateral-coupling signature (m74 isolated core4 max, others min vs model r69 +1.2 ambient): core4 meas 63 vs model 63.75 => residual -0.75 (model TOO HOT) neighbors: c5 +1.04, c6 +0.75, c1 +0.83, c2 -0.83, c0 -0.95 (mixed but hot-neighbor side +) Anti-correlation (hot core model too hot, cold neighbors model too cold) = MODEL LATERAL UNDER-COUPLING (real chip spreads laterally more than model). A sensor gain on core4 would make it read HIGHER; it reads LOWER => core4 NOT gain-faulted. NEXT decisive test: do c1,c2,c3,c6 (high excess in multi-core configs) show it in ISOLATED self-heating? - if isolated self-heating MATCHES model => NO sensor gain; it's all lateral model error. - if isolated reads HIGH => real sensor gain on that core. Expected isolated residual if k% gain ~ k*model_rise(~16C): k=8% -> +1.3C. Measuring isolated core1, core2, core3, core6 next.
